title: Ease On Down and the Saratoga Club on Lenox Avenue
summary: Barbarin says Ease On Down was a feature at the Saratoga Club, where he enjoyed the shows, and discusses Teddy Hill and Bob Williams.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Because we all was working together. Well let's play Ease On Down.
This is Brunswick by Louis Russell and his orchestra.
Yeah, but in the books I mean... They have a case on down, but it's wrong.
Yeah. The books are wrong again. Well I'll tell you. Don't pay in the kitchen the books.

You see that tune there, Ease On Down? That was one of our feature tunes at the Saratoga Club. When we were at Saratoga Club. On Annex Avenue. Yeah. We was waiting for Casper Holstein then. Casper Holstein, he was in the undertaking business. And he had a club also, you know. Saratoga Club. I enjoyed working at that club. Also, enjoyed playing the shows there. Very good show. I love to play shows. Oh, I just like music, period. That's all. Okay, we got the music. It's good. That's Greta Walton.
Was Teddy Hill much of a tenor solo player?

Yeah, it sounds very good. Gee, good, man. He's on down.
